We've only been in pads for two days,” Bowles said. “We're not concerned at this point, and I think those things take care of themselves. Once you get past two or three preseason games, you start to worry a little bit. Right now, there are a lot of contracts getting done. There are a lot of people in camp that's sitting in or holding in. There are a lot of people nicked up. We go about business as usual. He's been very engaged, and he's been great."

title: Often don't have a great view of OL-DL 1-on-1's, but that wasn't the case today as they happened right in front of us. Here are some notes: • Good showing from the tackles. Thought Jermaine Eluemunor won both of his reps against Abdul Carter and Brian Burns. Basically swallowed them up on bull rushes. Thought Andrew Thomas won against Carter and Burns as well. As he often does, Thomas used his athleticism to run them around the pocket. • Kayvon Thibodeaux beat Jon Runyan with an inside move. Runyan fared better against Shelby Harris. • Jon Michael Schmitz and DJ Reader split their reps. • Francis Mauigoa held up well against Darius Alexander. The period closed with Mauigoa stopping Abdul Carter. Carter asked for another rep immediately and beat Mauigoa with a swipe that had the rookie doing a full spin. Overall, solid showing for the O-line considering the drill is tilted toward the defense.
summary:
Often don't have a great view of OL-DL 1-on-1's, but that wasn't the case today as they happened right in front of us. Here are some notes:

• Good showing from the tackles. Thought Jermaine Eluemunor won both of his reps against Abdul Carter and Brian Burns. Basically swallowed them up on bull rushes. Thought Andrew Thomas won against Carter and Burns as well. As he often does, Thomas used his athleticism to run them around the pocket.

• Kayvon Thibodeaux beat Jon Runyan with an inside move. Runyan fared better against Shelby Harris.

• Jon Michael Schmitz and DJ Reader split their reps. 

• Francis Mauigoa held up well against Darius Alexander. The period closed with Mauigoa stopping Abdul Carter. Carter asked for another rep immediately and beat Mauigoa with a swipe that had the rookie doing a full spin. 

Overall, solid showing for the O-line considering the drill is tilted toward the defense.

• Kayvon Thibodeaux beat Jon Runyan with an inside move. Runyan fared better against Shelby Harris.

title: Practice report here today: • Lot of load management. JuJu Smith-Schuster was held out of practice with knee swelling, while Darius Slayton and Malachi Fields got little (if any) work in team periods. That led to an increase in first-team reps for Odell, who had one catch in 11-on-11 periods. He looks like he still has some juice, but has yet to make an impact in camp. Marcus Mbow rotated with Andrew Thomas at left tackle. • Another practice where Jaxson Dart didn't look particularly sharp. He had a red-zone TD pass to TE Isaiah Likely that went through the hands of slot CB Dru Phillips. The scrambling in the final red zone situation was tough. Dart's legs are a weapon and he did have open space, but defenders' gripes about QB runs when they can't hit him are valid. The Giants had a first down at the defense's 18-yard line with 42 seconds left trailing by six points. Dart hit Likely on a 7-yard out route and then scrambled 10 yards for a first down. With first-and-goal at the 3, he over-threw Odell on a fade and had a pass batted down (I think by Darius Alexander). Then on third-and-goal he scrambled in for an easy TD and flipped the ball into Greg Newsome's face. Newsome wasn't happy, but Isaiah Likely was there and quickly stepped in to prevent anything from escalating. • Deonte Banks continues to rotate at corner with the first-team defense. I view the starting corner positions as totally up for grabs. • Solid day for Ben Sauls who made 10-of-12 field goals. • The Giants did a 9-on-7 period. That is tailor made for Patrick Ricard and he delivered some thundering lead blocks. • Dalen Cambre is quietly having a strong camp. He's going to need to make the roster on special teams, but he has been showing his reliability as a receiver. • Jason Pinnock had an interception on a Jameis Winston pass that was thrown right to him. • Got a good look at Chris Snee working with the offensive line during indy drills. Saw him tutoring Francis Mauigoa. Snee spends a lot of time working 1-on-1 with international OL Jarrod Gray. The Giants continue to take things very slowly with Gray, who doesn't get reps in team drills.

title: If we’re reading potential federal law literally — and why not? — then the PCSA is defining eligibility period as “maximum of five calendar years” from enrollment (or academic year following 19th birthday). A calendar year is commonly defined as January 1-December 31, which means a literal reading of the bill means not being eligible past December 31 of their fifth academic year. And even if it’s defined as five consecutive 12-month periods of eligibility, what about a football player who enrolls as a freshman in early January? Would that make him ineligible under federal law from playing in a mid-January national championship game in his 5th year? What if a freshman enrolled January 5, 2026? Would that make him ineligible from playing in a NCG on January 6, 2031?

- OLB Khalil Mack consistently pressured the quarterback throughout practice.

Isaiah Likely caught a Dart TD pass that was tipped by Dru Phillips #talkinball

title: #Giants camp takeaways .. - A promotion for Odell Beckham Jr. He worked with the starting rotation of Darnell Mooney & Calvin Austin. He’s been getting open in camp. Just not getting thrown the ball. Clearly coaches rewarding that. Odell caught two passes on Tuesday (one in 11 on 11, another in 7 on 7). He was targeted four times. - It was another eh day for the offense. Jaxson Dart finished 6 of 14 with a TD run and throw (more on that below). This is now quite the string of uninspiring practices from them. You’d like to see this snapped soon. - The starters did score their first touchdowns of the summer. One in a red-zone period. Dart got Isaiah Likely from ~ five yards out. That’s the good. The bad: It was the only TD from the starters in 11 red zone plays (working their way in starting at the 15). - The offense also scored a TD when Dart ran it in from three yards out in a drive that started at the 18 going in. He then threw the ball off Greg Newsome’s helmet, which almost started a scuffle. - Penalties were again an issue. Can’t blame the rain today. There were six called. Just sloppy. So many of them pre-snap, too (five ).

title: Tanner McKee on the QB2 competition: "It's the NFL. Every year that I've been here, we've had four quarterbacks, got to compete for a job. That's nothing new. ...Every year I think you're going to compete on the spot. And so yeah, I'm looking forward." On if he was surprised after being the clear QB2 last year: "I don't think you could be surprised whenever they bring in somebody or there's ever a competition, because it's kind of like what we're saying in the NFL: There's always going to be competition. They're trying to improve the roster every year, and so anybody that they can bring in to make you compete or make you earn your spot, that's that's definitely what everybody wants. And for a player, it's great. It is great to have somebody to push you and to and to make you better, and you know the stakes in practice are a little bit higher, and so it makes it fun. Honestly, he's great."
